record.paper_title: New results and open problems on subgraph centrality
record.original_question: Let A be a non-diagonalizable n × n matrix with nonnegative algebraic entries, regarded as the adjacency matrix of a weighted directed graph G, and let β ≠ 0 be an algebraic number. If two vertices i and j satisfy [e^{βA}]_{ii} = [e^{βA}]_{jj}, must i and j be cospectral? Equivalently, prove or disprove that the cospectrality conclusion from the diagonalizable case still holds without assuming diagonalizability or special restrictions on the Jordan form.

evidence.quote: Problem 1. Let A be a (non diagonalizable) n × n matrix, whose entries are all nonnegative algebraic numbers, regarded as the adjacency matrix of a weighted directed graph G. Let β 6= 0 be an algebraic number. Prove or disprove the following statement: if for two vertices i, j we have [e^{βA}]_{ii} = [e^{βA}]_{jj}, then i and j are cospectral.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be an $n \times n$ matrix all of whose entries are nonnegative algebraic numbers, viewed as the adjacency matrix of a weighted directed graph $G$ on vertex set $\{1,\dots,n\}$, and assume that $A$ is not diagonalizable. Let $\beta$ be a nonzero algebraic number, and consider the matrix exponential $e^{\beta A} = \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \frac{(\beta A)^k}{k!}$.

Two vertices $i$ and $j$ of $G$ are called cospectral (with respect to $A$) if the principal submatrices obtained by deleting row and column $i$ and by deleting row and column $j$ have the same characteristic polynomial; equivalently, the closed-walk generating functions $[A^k]_{ii} = [A^k]_{jj}$ for every nonnegative integer $k$.

Prove or disprove: if $[e^{\beta A}]_{ii} = [e^{\beta A}]_{jj}$ for two vertices $i,j$, then $i$ and $j$ are cospectral.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicit open problem in the 2021/2023 work on subgraph centrality, asking whether the cospectrality conclusion known in the diagonalizable case extends to general non-diagonalizable nonnegative algebraic adjacency matrices. A web search did not turn up any subsequent paper resolving this case; the diagonalizable case (Estrada's conjecture) has been proven, but the non-diagonalizable extension appears unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Vertex distinction with subgraph centrality: A proof of Estrada's conjecture and some generalizations
status_evidence.snippet: Proves Estrada's conjecture in the diagonalizable case: equal diagonal entries of e^{βA} imply cospectrality.
status_evidence.claim: The diagonalizable case is solved; the non-diagonalizable extension remains the stated open problem.

status_evidence.title: New results and open problems on subgraph centrality (zbMATH 7676345)
status_evidence.snippet: Lists Problem 1 asking to prove or disprove the cospectrality implication for non-diagonalizable nonnegative algebraic adjacency matrices.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly listed as an open problem.
